transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a laundry and dry cleaners, and lately... it's just getting out of hand. The tickets, the receipts, my workshop notes, and the actual customer jobs all just end up piled together. It gets to the point where I look at the mess and I just do not know what to handle first.
Have you always had trouble staying organized and keeping track of tasks like this since you were younger, or is this something that's changed recently compared to how you used to function?

No, it's not really a new thing. I've pretty much always been this way. Um... even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was a bright kid, but just really scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my papers, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my work. So, yeah, it's always been like this for me.
Growing up, did you also tend to be very restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or act impulsively—like blurting things out or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Um, I'm not really sure about the restless part. I mean, I know I talked out of turn a lot, like I just mentioned, but I don't really remember having a lot of trouble sitting still or... or making quick decisions without thinking. If I did, I guess I just didn't notice it, or maybe nobody made a big deal out of it compared to me losing my papers all the time. I mostly just remember them saying I was scattered.

Besides your struggles at work, do you notice this same kind of disorganization and difficulty focusing in other parts of your life right now—like at home, managing finances, or in personal relationships?

Well, at the shop it's definitely causing real issues. Because of the mess, we've had late orders, the billing gets all confused, and... honestly, it leads to some pretty tense moments with the rest of the staff and the customers. 

And outside of work... yeah, it happens there, too. Like at my church. I actually had to step back from leading some of the planning we do there. I just couldn't keep it all straight, and people were getting frustrated with me.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset, pervasive inattentive symptoms (disorganization, losing materials, difficulty finishing tasks) across multiple settings (work, church) support ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. No history of hyperactivity/impulsivity argues against hyperkinetic conduct disorder (F90.1). Lack of personality pathology or psychotic features rules out F60.8 and F29.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong pattern beginning in childhood (documented by teachers) of significant inattentive symptoms—disorganization, losing important materials, difficulty completing tasks, distractibility, and talking out of turn—without prominent hyperactive or impulsive features such as motor restlessness or impulsive decision-making.
